text: We have already seen in Section 7.1 an example of a relational schema that is not in BCNF: in_dep (ID, name, salary, dept_name, building, budget) The functional dependency dept_name — budget holds on in_dep, but dept_name is not a superkey (because a department may have a number of different instructors). In Section 7.1 we saw that the decomposition of in_dep into instructor and department is a better design. The instructor schema is in BCNF. All of the nontrivial functional dependencies that hold, such as: ID — name, dept_name, salary include ID on the left side of the arrow, and ID is a superkey (actually, in this case, the primary key) for instructor. (In other words, there is no nontrivial functional depen- dency with any combination of name, dept_name, and salary, without ID, on the left side.) Thus, instructor is in BCNF. Similarly, the department schema is in BCNF because all of the nontrivial functional dependencies that hold, such as: dept_name — building, budget include dept_ name on the left side of the arrow, and dept_name is a superkey (and the primary key) for department. Thus, department is in BCNF.
